title: Rumesh Triumphs in Ostrava with Another Massive Throw
summary: Sri Lanka’s javelin sensation, Rumesh Tharanga Pathiragae, continued his golden run in Europe by clinching the gold medal at the Ostrava Golden Spike competition in the Czech Republic with a throw of 86.57m. Competing in this World Athletics Continental Tour Gold event, the 23‑year‑old opened with 85.87m, improved to 86.30m on his second attempt, and sealed victory with 86.57m on his third. That effort was more than enough to secure the top spot. Double World Champion Anderson Peters of Grenada finished second with 84.27m, while South Africa’s Douw Smit claimed third with 83.90m. Earlier this month in Rome, Rumesh stunned the athletics world with a throw of 92.62m, making him the 8th best thrower of all time. In Ostrava, unlike Rome, he entered as the clear favorite, the “man to beat” in world javelin this year. He was even featured as the face of the competition during the pre‑event press conference alongside US Olympic pole vault champion Katie Moon. Currently ranked third in the world, Rumesh owns the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 5th best throws of the season. He is the first Sri Lankan athlete in history to achieve such a high global ranking in a specific event, marking a new era of dominance for Sri Lankan athletics. Following Ostrava, Rumesh will compete in the Diamond League in Doha before returning home. Next month, he is set to represent Sri Lanka at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland.

title: Ananda Ends 23-Year Wait with Historic Victory Over St. Thomas’ College
summary: Ananda College Rugby produced one of the most memorable moments in the school’s sporting history by defeating St. Thomas’ College and ending a 23-year wait for victory over the Mount Lavinia outfit in the Schools Rugby League encounter played at Rajagiriya. The landmark triumph is more than just a win. It is the latest chapter in a remarkable resurgence that has transformed Ananda into one of the most courageous and competitive teams in Division ‘A’ rugby this season. Having returned to the top division after a lengthy absence, many observers expected Ananda to struggle against the established powerhouses. Instead, the Maroon and Gold warriors have earned admiration across the rugby fraternity for their fearless approach, commitment, and fighting spirit. Week after week, they have challenged stronger and more experienced opponents, refusing to be intimidated by reputation or history. This victory over St. Thomas’ is a fitting reward for a team that has consistently punched above its weight throughout the season. While the league table may not fully reflect their performances, several narrow defeats in the opening weeks denied Ananda the opportunity of securing a place in the Cup Segment. Those close losses, often decided by the finest of margins, masked the true quality of this young side. Many rugby followers would agree that based on performances alone, Ananda deserved to be among the Cup Segment contenders. The team’s ability to compete with the best schools in the country, despite being newcomers to Division ‘A’, has been one of the stories of the 2026 season. The victory against St. Thomas’ also underlines the remarkable progress achieved by the coaching staff, management, players, and supporters who have worked tirelessly to rebuild the rugby programme. What has stood out most is the character of the players. Time and again they have shown resilience, determination, and an unwavering belief in their ability to compete at the highest level. title: Shanaka, Mishara fifties set up series-levelling win for Sri Lanka
summary: Dasun Shanaka produced the batting ballistics, Kamil Mishara held the innings together, and Sri Lanka’s spinners dominated the middle overs, comfortably defending their 194 for 6. This 37-run victory brings Sri Lanka level 1-1 in the series against West Indies, with one match to play on Sunday night. Sri Lanka had been struggling at 88 for 4 in the 13th over when Shanaka joined Mishara at the crease. The pair then blasted 103 off 42 balls together to propel Sri Lanka to a commanding score of 194 for 6, hitting seven sixes and nine fours between them. Although Sri Lanka struck twice with the new ball, West Indies had still looked confident in pursuit at 89 for 2, until Sri Lanka’s spinners went to work. A run out would spark a collapse that cost West Indies six wickets for 32 runs. They struggled to recover from 122 for 8 after 15 overs. Dushmantha Chameera, who had struck early in the innings and was effective in the other phases as well, closed out the match in the 19th over, taking three wickets for 9 runs. West Indies were 157 all out, despite Rovman Powell and Shimron Hetmyer having put on 81 off 47 for the third wicket. Although he arrived at the crease with Sri Lanka in some trouble, Shanaka was almost immediately aggressive, blasting Roston Chase’s offspin onto the roof of the Sabina Park stadium fourth ball, before crashing him for a four and thumping another six next ball. All three of these boundaries came through deep midwicket. He also struck a huge six down the ground, and hooked a ball over fine leg as well, as he stormed to a 19-ball fifty. This equalled his own record for fastest Sri Lanka men’s half century in T20Is. title: Rumesh to Compete in Ostrava on Tuesday
summary: By Anjana Kaluarachchi After his heroic performance in Rome that made world headlines, javelin thrower Rumesh Tharanga will head to the Czech Republic to compete in the Golden Ostrava on Tuesday, 16 June, a World Athletics Continental Tour Gold event. Tharanga, who threw 92.62m to become the 8thbest thrower of all time, will once again face double world champion Anderson Peters of Grenada and former Olympic gold medalist Thomas Röhler of Germany, among other top competitors. Unlike in Rome, Rumesh will enter the competition as the favorite, carrying the tag of ‘man to beat’ in world javelin this year. The 23-year-old former Peterite is currently ranked third in the world and owns the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 5thbest throws of the season. He is the first Sri Lankan athlete in history to achieve such a high global ranking in a specific event, marking a new level of world dominance for Sri Lankan athletics. Following his heroic performance in Rome, Tharanga stayed in Italy for a week, training in both Rome and Milan, before departing for the Czech Republic yesterday. Following Ostrava, Tharanga will compete in the Diamond League in Doha before returning to Sri Lanka. Next month, he will head to Scotland to represent the country at the Commonwealth Games.

title: SL Star Rumesh Tharanga Rises to 3rd in World Rankings
summary: Sri Lanka’s javelin sensation Rumesh Tharanga has stunned the athletics world, rising to third place in the global javelin throw rankings after his monster throw of 92.62m at the Rome Diamond League. With that performance, Tharanga has now amassed 1,324 ranking points, placing him just behind Germany’s Julian Weber and Grenada’s Anderson Peters. Notably, he is the youngest athlete in the world’s top 20, underscoring his rapid rise and extraordinary potential. A Historic Milestone for Sri Lanka Tharanga’s achievement marks a historic milestone for Sri Lankan athletics, as he becomes the highest-ranked male athlete from the nation in world athletics standings. He has also emerged as Asia’s top-ranked javelin thrower, overtaking India’s Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra. The 23-year-old’s record-breaking performance in Rome  not only secured his maiden Diamond League victory but also set a new national record, a meet record, and reaffirmed his position as the world leader this season. Historic Throw in Rome Just days after making his Diamond League debut in Rabat, where he finished second, Tharanga soared past the 90m mark for the first time in Rome. His colossal effort on the second attempt sealed his place in history, making him the 8th best javelin thrower of all time since the introduction of the new javelin specification in 1986. Remarkably, Tharanga now owns the first, second, third, and fifth best throws of 2026, cementing his status as the man to beat this season. He is also the only thrower to surpass 92m since Arshad Nadeem’s gold medal-winning throw at the 2024 Paris Olympics. From Kalutara to Global Stardom Born in Kalutara, Tharanga’s journey has been extraordinary. Initially a schoolboy cricketer and fast bowler clocking 134 km/h, he switched to throwing events under the guidance of his father, a former discus and shot-put athlete. title: Chamari, Vishmi Power Sri Lanka to Comfortable Win over Pakistan
summary: Skipper Chamari Athapaththu fell just short of what could have been a magnificent century, but her blistering 94 ensured Sri Lanka cruised to a comfortable victory over Pakistan in their ICC Women’s T20 World Cup warm-up match at Derby today. Pakistan, batting first, posted 168 for 8, with Chethana Vimukthi starring for Sri Lanka’s bowling attack by claiming 4 for 31. In reply, Athapaththu and 20 year old Vishmi Gunarathne forged a commanding 159-run opening stand that all but sealed the game. Athapaththu, attempting to reach her century with a six, was dismissed for 94 off 58 balls  an innings decorated with nine fours and five sixes. Gunarathne, who showed intent early in the powerplay with a flurry of boundaries, remained unbeaten on 63 from 50 deliveries, striking four fours and three sixes. Her composed knock perfectly complemented Athapaththu’s fireworks, guiding Sri Lanka to a dominant finish.
